title: PDF Fusion Pro: a private PDF merge and unlock dashboard
summary: A Streamlit dashboard that merges, reorders, password-protects and unlocks PDFs in memory, without saving files to disk.

brief.problem: Free online PDF mergers ask you to upload contracts and payslips to a server you know nothing about. For legal or financial documents, that is a real privacy risk.
brief.goal: Build a merge tool where privacy is the default: files are handled in memory, nothing is stored, the result can be password-protected, and you see page counts and sizes before you merge.

mine: Sole developer: planned the features, wrote the merge, unlock and password logic, and designed the dark dashboard.
Built and deployed it over one weekend.

process.text: Looked at why people use online mergers and what they give up. Decided the tool should run on the user's own machine and keep files in memory only.
A control panel for the output name and password, a queue table with pages and size per file, summary numbers on top, and one clear Merge button.
pypdf reads and joins the files in memory. A drag-and-drop list sets the order. An optional password protects the merged file. Nothing is written to disk.
Added an Unlock tab for PDFs where you know the password. It tells you if a file is open, restricted or password-protected before it tries.
Run it on your own machine and nothing leaves it. The hosted demo runs on Streamlit's servers, so try it with sample files only.
